what_its_for: Lumateperone is used to treat schizophrenia in adults. It is also used to treat depressive episodes that happen with bipolar disorder (bipolar I or bipolar II) in adults, either alone or together with lithium or valproate (mood stabilizers).
how_to_take: Take lumateperone by mouth, with or without food. Swallow the capsule whole — do not crush, chew, or open it. Try to take it at the same time each day to help you remember. Do not take more than your doctor prescribed.
dosing: The usual dose is one 42 mg capsule taken once daily. Your doctor will decide the right dose for you based on your condition and other medicines you take. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions and never change your dose on your own.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember on that same day. If it is already the next day, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at the regular time. Never take two doses in one day to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store lumateperone at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep it away from moisture and heat. Store in the original container with the lid tightly closed. Keep this medicine out of reach of children and pets. Do not use it after the expiration date on the label.
what_to_avoid: Avoid drinking alcohol while taking this medicine, as it can increase dizziness and drowsiness. Do not drive, operate heavy machinery, or do activities that require alertness until you know how this medicine affects you. Avoid taking other medicines that make you drowsy without asking your doctor first. Tell your doctor about ALL other medicines, vitamins, and supplements you take, as some medicines can interact with lumateperone, especially certain antifungals, antibiotics, or seizure medications.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you experience: thoughts of suicide or self-harm, new or worsening depression or anxiety, uncontrolled muscle movements in your face, tongue, or body (which could be a sign of tardive dyskinesia), very stiff muscles, high fever, sweating, or confusion (possible signs of a rare but serious condition called neuroleptic malignant syndrome), fainting or feeling like your heart is racing, significant weight gain, increased thirst or urination (possible signs of high blood sugar), or severe dizziness when standing up. Also tell your doctor if you feel restless and cannot sit still.
when_it_works: Some people may notice improvements in symptoms within the first 1 to 2 weeks, but it may take 4 to 6 weeks or longer to feel the full benefit of this medicine. Do not stop taking it even if you feel better, unless your doctor tells you to. Stopping suddenly can make your condition worse.
special_populations: Older adults (65 and over): Use with caution. Older adults with dementia-related psychosis should NOT take this medicine, as it may increase the risk of death. Pregnancy: Talk to your doctor if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant. Babies born to mothers who took antipsychotic medicines in the last trimester of pregnancy may have withdrawal symptoms or muscle problems after birth. Breastfeeding: It is not known if lumateperone passes into breast milk. Talk to your doctor before breastfeeding. Liver problems: If you have moderate to severe liver disease, this medicine may not be right for you. Your doctor will check if it is safe for you. Children: This medicine is not approved for use in children.
